newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba rejects U.S. hijack trial allegations.
newsitem.headline: Cuba rejects U.S. hijack trial allegations.

text.p: Cuba on Thursday rejected allegations made in a U.S. court that an accused Palestinian hijacker diverted a Havana-bound Spanish airliner to Miami because he did not want to go to Cuba for military training.

Saad'o Mohamed Ibrahim Intissar faces air piracy charges for the July 26, 1996, hijacking. His attorney said on Tuesday he had forced Iberia Flight 6621 to fly to Miami because he did not want to go to Cuba where he had been sent by an anti-Israeli group for military training.
Asked to comment on this, Cuba's acting Foreign Ministry spokesman, Alejandro Gonzalez, said: "The reasons for which this plane was hijacked have absolutely nothing to do with Cuba."

He went on to note that the trial was being held in Miami, where he said the issue of Cuba is "usually politicized." This was a reference to the presence in Miami of a big community of Cuban exiles opposed to Cuba's one-party communist government.
"Evidently, the (accused's) defence lawyer thinks that by using the Cuba theme he can gain some advantage for his client," the Cuban spokesman said, without elaborating.

Intissar's attorney, Joaquin Mendez, said the accused was sent to Cuba by a group called the Islamic Revolutionary Army, which he said was connected to the Iranian-supported Hizbollah organisation. Intissar is accused of using a fake bomb and a makeshift knife to force the jet to land in Miami.
